messages.author: 6c4d187713e325b8
messages.subject: MIRT Simulation diagnostics Function
parts:
Loving the MIRTCAT Package, thanks for all your work Phil! 

I was wondering if anyone has written code for more detailed post-simulation metrics? E.g., stats outputs of performance and rendering visualisation with GGPlot. Ideally it would be great to also be able to subset this by a criterion (when supplied; e.g., item content domains "content_prop"; or participant demographics [although ideally this would not show much difference under non-dif items]). 

This is likely all possible using the output already contained within the Mirt Cat object in addition to a few other calculations, however, it would be nice to not reinvent the wheel if much of the code for this post-simulation diagnostics already exists. If not, this chain could provide some ideas / code for future researchers interested in simulation-diagnostics. 

Although this could be dreaming, Many of these could also be utilised post-Shiny administration to also diagnose how the CAT went with real participant data. 

Some I had in mind were: 

Performance metrics such as:
Efficiency
Average Number of Items Administered
Time reduction  / average item reduction 
Bias
MSE
RMSE
Pearson Correlation Coef between true theta and Cat estimates, and between CAT estimated and simply taking the mean of all items (e.g., the standard approach using Classical test theory)
Total % who met stop criteria

Error metrics such as:
Mean SE
Min SE
Max SE
Std. Dev. of SE
% < certain thresholds, e.g., % <= 0.30, % <= 0.25,  % <= 0.15

Some Visualisations (each could also have range/sd bar options):
Item number or ID vs Frequency of administration
Theta (X) vs average # of items (Y) 
Average Final Ability Estimate vs Simulated θ 
Average Standard Error vs Final Ability Estimate 
Average Test Information vs Final Ability Estimate

Kind Regards,
    Conal

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: MIRT Simulation diagnostics Function
parts:
Hi Conal,

I have not added information like this to the mirtCAT package, largely because I think it would make the code-base in the package slightly more difficult to follow (functions like RMSE/bias etc would be a little distracting to sift through). I have, however, written the SimDesign package to perform more general purpose Monte Carlo simulation experiments, where on the wiki I have examples that use mirtCAT. There's lots of features in the SimDesign package which IMHO are essential for evaluating simulations, and making ggplot2 graphics afterwards is rather straightforward since the results will always be in a tibble format. 

That said, from your list there still would need to be a number of customized functions to add, which I suppose could be added to mirtCAT in something like a summary() output. I'll have to think about what to do in this context as there would be a great deal of information that could be reported, so it would be hard to strike the right balance between good information and TMI. 

Phil

messages.author: 6c4d187713e325b8
messages.subject: Re: MIRT Simulation diagnostics Function
parts:
Hi Phil,
  Thanks for the run down and the link to SimDesign which has most of these functions. I agree that it has excellent features, including the tibble output for passing to GGplot for plotting much of what is needed. I can recommend this approach for anyone wishing to go down this line.  

Several people have reached out with ideas and codes for simulation analysis (thanks). These involve extracting particular parameters from each simulated participant (e.g., items administered, parameter estimates, etc) and combining them into a tibble for plotting or calculating correlations/error. Everything is already nicely in the mirt object so the desired parameters can be extracted through loops. 

I found SimDesign could do most things, with the custom code from the mirt object doing the rest :) 

With Kind Regards,
    Conal
